chapter: Fletcher as a leader and early bandmates
title: Insert on Benny Carter's marking of arrangements
summary: Carter marked phrasing and shading in his charts, demonstrated on his horn, and had a satisfied smile when the band played it well.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: ... in his arrangements, and how he wants them played, how he wants this phrased. And if you don't get the idea of what he's talking about, he'll take his horn and show you. His marks are very thorough, how he wants you to do his correct shading, and there he was a dinger at having the right tempo for his arrangements. And he'll play them back. When you finish with that particular arrangement, you could almost play it with your eyes closed -- he was that thorough.
Then you would see the smile that meant satisfaction. Otherwise, if you weren't doing the job, you saw another type of smile, and it wasn't welcome.
